The Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) programs, as outlined in 34 CFR Part 682, include four programs that enable students or their parents to pay for the costs of attending postsecondary schools (§682.100(A)). These programs are: the Stafford Loan Program, the PLUS Program, the SLS Program, and the Consolidation Loan Program (§682.100(A)). 

A guaranty agency guarantees a lender against losses due to default by the borrower on a FFEL loan, and if the guaranty agency meets certain Federal requirements, it is reimbursed by the Secretary for all or part of the amount of default claims it pays to lenders (§682.100(b)(1)). 

The Secretary may require a school to repay funds paid to other program participants or purchase from the holder of a FFEL loan that portion of the loan that is unenforceable, if the Secretary determines that the payment or disbursement resulted from the school's violation of a Federal statute or regulation, or the school's negligent or willful false certification (§682.609(1)). 

A school must maintain records for each Stafford, SLS, or PLUS loan received by or on behalf of its students, including a copy of the loan certification or data electronically submitted to the lender (§682.610(1)). 

A guaranty agency must establish and submit to the Secretary for approval procedures to ensure that consolidation loans are not an excessive proportion of the guaranty agency's recoveries on defaulted loans (§682.401(20)).

what is the maximum amount a student can.answer:
The maximum amount a student can borrow varies depending on the type of loan and the student's level of study. 

For Federal Perkins Loans and NDSLs, the maximum annual amount is $5,500 for undergraduate students and $8,000 for graduate or professional students (34 CFR §674.12(a)). The aggregate unpaid principal amount may not exceed $27,500 for undergraduate students who have completed two years of a program, $60,000 for graduate or professional students, and $11,000 for other students (34 CFR §674.12(b)).

For Stafford Loans, the aggregate unpaid principal amount may not exceed $73,000 for undergraduate study, and $138,500 for graduate or professional students, including loans for undergraduate study (34 CFR §682.204(d)(5) and 34 CFR §685.203(d)(3)).

For Direct Subsidized Loans, the aggregate unpaid principal amount may not exceed $23,000 for undergraduate students and $65,500 for graduate or professional students (34 CFR §685.203(d)(1) and (2)).

For Direct Unsubsidized Loans, the aggregate unpaid principal amount may not exceed $31,000 for dependent undergraduate students, $57,500 for independent undergraduate students, and $138,500 for graduate or professional students (34 CFR §685.203(e)(1), (2), and (3)). 

In general, the total amount a student may borrow for any academic year of study may not exceed the student's cost of attendance less other estimated financial assistance for that student (34 CFR §685.301(a)(6)).
